sources.title: Review of pediatric obstructive sleep apnea phenotypes (Children 2023;10(6):955)
sources.supports: OSA affects about 2–5% of the general pediatric population; adenotonsillar hypertrophy dominates in preschoolers, obesity in adolescents; a congenital-structural phenotype (e.g., Down syndrome) is present from early life.

recommendation_ka: დაუნის სინდრომისას ობსტრუქციული ძილის აპნოეს რისკი ძალიან მაღალია (ერთ კოჰორტაში 81%) შუა სახის ჰიპოპლაზიის, მაკროგლოსიის, ზედა სასუნთქი გზების დაქვეითებული ტონუსისა და სიმსუქნის გამო; სხეულის მასის ინდექსი და ხვრინვის/აპნოეს სიმპტომები უფრო მძიმე ფორმას წინასწარმეტყველებს. ასეთ ბავშვებში დაბალია ზღურბლი პოლისომნოგრაფიისთვის.

sources.supports: OSA found in 81% of children with Down syndrome; BMI and snoring/apnoea symptoms predicted higher AHI.

sources.title: ERS statement on obstructive sleep disordered breathing in 1- to 23-month-old children
sources.supports: Current edition: based on systematic review of 159 articles; oSDB in infants is multifactorial; predisposing conditions include mandibular hypoplasia; complex conditions such as Down syndrome and Prader-Willi syndrome benefit from treatment.

sources.title: Diagnosis and management of childhood obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (Pediatrics 2012)
sources.supports: Current edition: for uncomplicated OSAS (adenotonsillar hypertrophy and/or obesity in otherwise healthy child). Screen for snoring; adenotonsillectomy first line when adenotonsillar hypertrophy; high-risk patients monitored as inpatients postoperatively; objective testing after therapy in high-risk or persistent symptoms; CPAP if AT not performed or OSAS persists; intranasal steroids an option for mild OSAS when AT contraindicated or mild postoperative OSAS.

sources.title: A randomized trial of adenotonsillectomy for childhood sleep apnea
sources.supports: Remains the current pivotal RCT: 464 children aged 5–9 years; no difference in primary attention/executive outcome at 7 months; AT improved behaviour, quality of life, symptoms and PSG; PSG normalised in 79% after AT vs 46% with watchful waiting; lower normalisation in Black and obese children.

sources.title: Adenotonsillectomy vs watchful waiting for childhood OSA — CHAT commentary
sources.supports: Commentary on the current pivotal CHAT trial: AHI changes after AT vs watchful waiting were modest; either approach considered a reasonable option in the studied population.
